title: One house, two houses
description: Make Portuguese nouns plural, from -s and -es to -ns, -ões and -ais, and make the words around them agree.

guide.summary: Most Portuguese plurals add -s, but the last letter of the noun decides the exact ending. Learn the six endings and the article and adjective that change with the noun.

sections.title: Ending in a vowel: add -s
sections.text: A noun that ends in a vowel, stressed or not, nasal -ã included, simply adds -s. Nothing else changes, and an accent stays where it is.
steps: Look at the last letter of the noun.
If it is a vowel, add -s and keep any accent.
watch: The final vowel never changes: casa gives casas, never cases.
Portuguese marks the plural even after a number: três chaves.

sections.title: Ending in -r, -z or -s: add -es
sections.text: After -r and -z, and after an -s at the end of a stressed syllable, Portuguese adds -es, a whole extra syllable. A noun whose -s ending is unstressed does not change.
steps: Does the noun end in -r or -z? Add -es.
Does it end in -s? Find the stress.
Stressed on the last syllable, like mês or país: add -es.
Stressed earlier, like lápis or ônibus: leave it unchanged.

examples.en: I am staying here for two months.

watch: An accent may vanish in the new syllable: mês gives meses, inglês gives ingleses.
Never a bare -s after -r or -z: not mulhers, not luzs.

sections.title: Ending in -m: change to -ns
sections.text: Portuguese never writes -ms at the end of a word. A final -m becomes -n before the -s.
steps: Spot the final -m.
Replace it with -n and add -s.

examples.en: Three men are waiting for the bus.

watch: No extra vowel: homens, not homenes.
Adjectives follow the same rule: jovem gives jovens, bom gives bons.

sections.title: Ending in -ão: three plurals
sections.text: Most nouns in -ão take -ões. A short list takes -ães, and another short list just adds -s. The dictionary, and this deck, give the plural of every -ão word.

rows: most words, and every word in -ção

steps: Is the noun pão, cão or alemão? Use -ães.
Is it mão, irmão or cidadão? Just add -s.
Otherwise use -ões.
watch: Mães means mothers, from mãe; hands is mãos.
Every noun ending in -ção takes -ões: lição gives lições.

sections.title: Ending in -al, -ol, -ul: the -l becomes -is
sections.text: A final -l cannot stand before -s. After a, o or u it turns into -is. The -ol plural takes an accent to keep its open o.
steps: Spot the final -l and the vowel before it.
Drop the -l and add -is.
For -ol, write óis with an accent.

examples.pt: Ele lê dois jornais por dia.
examples.en: He reads two newspapers a day.

watch: Not the English -ls, not the Spanish -les: animais.
The Brazilian money follows the rule: um real, dez reais.

sections.title: Ending in -el and -il
sections.text: A stressed -el becomes -éis. For -il, find the stress: a stressed -il becomes -is, and an -il stressed earlier becomes -eis.
steps: For -el, write -éis.
For -il, find the stressed syllable.
Stressed -il: -is. Stressed earlier, usually with an accent: -eis.
watch: A written accent before -il, as in fácil or útil, shows the stress is early: use -eis.
Hotéis and papéis need the accent on the é.

sections.title: The words around the noun agree
sections.text: In Portuguese the article, the adjectives and the verb all follow the noun into the plural. Each word takes its own plural rule.
steps: Make the noun plural with its own rule.
Change the article: o to os, a to as, um to uns, uma to umas.
Make every adjective plural, by its own ending.
Make the verb plural: é to são, está to estão.
watch: A colour is an adjective and agrees too: carros azuis.
Uns and umas mean some: uns livros, some books.

steps: Check that the noun ends in a vowel.
Add -s and keep any accent.
Make the article and adjectives plural as well.
After -r or -z, add -es.
After a stressed -s, add -es and drop the accent if the stress no longer needs it.
After an unstressed -s, change nothing.
Spot the final -m.
Change it to -n and add -s.
Pão, cão, alemão: -ães.
Mão, irmão, cidadão: add -s.
Every other -ão word: -ões.
Spot the final -l after a, o or u.
Replace the -l with -is.
For -ol, write -óis.
Stressed -el: -éis.
Stressed -il: -is.
Unstressed -il, with the stress earlier: -eis.
Make the noun plural.
Change the article to os, as, uns or umas.
Make adjectives and the verb plural.

exercises.source: Nós temos duas ____ perto do mar.
exercises.hint: What letter does casa end in?
exercises.feedback: A noun ending in a vowel keeps that vowel and adds one letter.
exercises.explanation: Casa ends in the vowel -a, so the plural just adds -s: duas casas.

mistakes.why: Portuguese never swaps the final vowel to make a plural. The -a stays where it is and only a letter is added after it.
The ending -es is for nouns ending in a consonant such as -r or -z. Casa already ends in a vowel.

exercises.instruction: Write the plural of the word in brackets.
exercises.hint: Café ends in a stressed vowel. Does that change anything?
exercises.feedback: A stressed final vowel behaves like any other vowel.
exercises.explanation: Café ends in the vowel -é, so it simply adds -s and keeps its accent: os cafés.

mistakes.why: The extra -e is only for nouns ending in a consonant. Café ends in a vowel, stressed or not, so one letter is enough.
That is still the singular, but os and são tell you there are several.

exercises.hint: Chave ends in a vowel. Precisar takes de before a noun.

exercises.explanation: Chave ends in -e, so its plural adds -s: três chaves. Precisar is followed by de.

mistakes.why: The noun stayed singular after three. Unlike some languages, Portuguese marks the plural even after a number.
The plural is fine, but precisar needs de before a noun.

exercises.instruction: Make the sentence plural: several windows. Write the whole sentence.
exercises.hint: Four words change: the article, the noun, the verb and the adjective.
exercises.feedback: Every word that refers to the window has to become plural.
exercises.explanation: A becomes as, janela adds -s, está becomes estão and aberta adds -s: as janelas estão abertas.

mistakes.why: The article and the noun are plural, but the verb and the adjective still describe one window.
The article stayed singular. In front of a plural feminine noun the article also takes -s.
That is the original sentence, still about one window.

exercises.hint: Look at the noun after duas.
exercises.feedback: After a number above one, the noun is plural.
exercises.explanation: Maçã ends in the vowel -ã, so it just adds -s: duas maçãs.

mistakes.why: The noun is still singular after duas, two.
The ending -ães belongs to some nouns in -ão. Maçã ends in a plain -ã, which is a vowel and just adds one letter.

exercises.explanation: Mulher ends in the consonant -r, so its plural adds -es: as mulheres.

exercises.instruction: Write the plural of the word in brackets.

That is the singular, but muitas, many, asks for a plural.
